title: tri-sdk: unify retry-adapter templates and simplify streaming session surface
author: Marina Kline
release_notes: Backwards-compatible refactor: introduces a shared retry-adapter template for Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs, simplifies the streaming session-facing surface, and bumps SDK package versions. No behavioral breaking changes expected for existing callers.
description:
Motivation: We maintain three SDKs with slightly divergent credential/retry primitives and streaming ergonomics. That divergence causes repeated bug surface (auth token races, differing backoff defaults) and duplicated maintenance. This PR introduces a small, opinionated 'retry-adapter template' and a lightweight stream-surface shim implemented across the Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs to harmonize defaults and reduce duplicated logic.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds a RetryAdapter template (config-driven) that normalizes backoff windows, jitter, and retryable-status heuristics across languages.
- Standardizes session lease/heartbeat hints exposed by streaming handles so consumers can implement warmup/prefetch logic consistently.
- Introduces a minimal, language-idiomatic stream-surface shim that maps the low-level event frames to a consistent async/pull model in each SDK (async iterators in Python/TS, channel-based iterator in Go).
- Moves credential rotation hooks into a single well-documented handshake lifecycle so the token refresh race window is reduced.
- Bumps package versions: python 0.23.0, typescript 3.2.0, go 1.6.0 (patch/minor as appropriate).

Checklist: 
- [x] Design doc reviewed by SDK leads (referenced ENG-1129)
- [x] Unit tests added for each SDK's retry logic
- [x] Integration streaming tests exercising token rotation under load
- [x] Docs/changelog updated
- [x] Compatibility smoke tested (no breaking changes)

- commit 2: python SDK: implement RetryAdapter, async iterator shim, unit tests, version bump
- commit 3: typescript SDK: implement RetryAdapter, pullstream facade, fix backpressure handling, version bump
- commit 4: go SDK: implement RetryAdapter, channel iterator, fix connector heartbeat deadlock discovered in tests
- commit 5: redwood core: expose lightweight session lifecycle hook for consumable heartbeats
- commit 6: docs: changelog entries and migration notes

Small illustrative snippet (TS adapter wiring):
const defaultConfig = { baseDelayMs: 50, maxDelayMs: 2000, jitter: 0.25, retries: 6 };
const adapter = new RetryAdapter(defaultConfig, tokenProvider);

Compatibility notes: The adapter uses conservative defaults designed to reduce spurious retries for streaming frames (especially 429/503). Applications that intentionally relied on a very small baseDelay should opt into a legacy profile via RetryAdapter.fromProfile('legacy').

Testing notes / CI flakiness: Third-party CI revealed an intermittent failure in the TS integration tests related to stream-backpressure under Node 18. Root cause: an edge case where a queued heartbeat could starve the user-data queue when the consumer used sync iterators. Fix: adjust pullFacade to prioritize data frames and add a microtask yield before applying heartbeat backpressure. The test was flaky locally but is stable post-fix.

Review conversation (highlights):
- Arjun Patel (reviewer): "Nice consolidation. Two asks: 1) add explicit metrics labels (retry_profile) to the SDK telemetry hooks; 2) call out migration steps for customers using custom retry loops."
- Marina Kline (author): "Added telemetry labels in commit 4, updated upgrade-guide with migration snippet and example backoff profiles."
- Lena Sørensen (reviewer): "Go change LGTM but please add a brief comment explaining the select loop ordering in puller.go — it avoids a deadlock we saw in integration tests."
- Marina: "Added a code comment and a small unit test that asserts ordering semantics."
- Diego Ramos (reviewer): "Can we avoid exposing the entire adapter config object in the top-level client surface? We should prefer builder helpers."
- Marina: "Agreed — introduced builders in Python/TS and helper constructors in Go; retained full config for advanced use only."
- CI bot: "integration-stream-tests failed on first run (ts flaky test). Rerun queued."
- CI bot (rerun): "All checks passed."

Merge decision: Squash-merge after reviewers approved and CI passed. No follow-up tasks blocked.

Follow-ups (future work):
- Introduce a lightweight opentracing label for retry attempts to correlate with upstream load (ENG-1382).
- Explore adaptive retry profiles based on observed latency to reduce tail-costs.
- Consider backfilling this adapter into the internal 'dedicated' runtime SDK if we see benefits in load tests.

If you want to try the new behavior locally: see docs/sdk/upgrade-guide.md section "try the unified retry adapter" for quickstart snippets per-language.
